messages.subject: refactoring nuts_givenmass and nuts_nondiag
parts:
Yuanjun: Has the dust settled on how you want to do the
adaptation in nuts_nondiag so that we could release if
we have to? Code shouldn't be merged with the master branch
until this is the case.

I didn't see any changes to our doc to reflect
nuts_nondiag.

Daniel and I are refactoring the mcmc classes right now
to use Eigen and in a few other ways.

We noticed some things that need to be fixed for
nuts_givenmass and nuts_nondiag:

0. There's no doc for it yet, and that needs to be done
before a release.

1. We need to merge these into a single file
where the mass is adapted in one case and set in the
other case. I'd rather just call this nuts_mass
and maybe change nuts_diag to nuts_mass_diag.
Ideally, we'd also roll these two files together to
cut down on cut-and-paste.

2. We need to change the constructor in nuts_givenmass to
take in either (a) a matrix, or (b) a var_context.
it should be the job of the client to nuts_givenmass

For 2, we don't want any file-based interfaces. One reason
is that we need to be able to call from R and that won't
be done by file.

And further, we want to:

3. Refactor nuts_diag to use a mass matrix formulation rather
than varying step sizes.

and

4. Integrate the parameters into RStan. We should only do
this after 1--2 are done.

- Bob

Great. It it's ready to go, the rest of this is
just the steps we need to take to get the documentation
and RStan ready to go.

Can you write up a short note on what you did for
adaptation? I'd like to include a description in the manual.

than 100 parameters and found it didn't work? This we should
talk about at the Stan meeting.

So on "master", I just pushed once without doing any further modification. Actually it will be great if you can remove the branch "nondiag_mass".

user's manual. So that means documenting the command-line
options.

>>
>
> Again, what does it mean for "doc"? I am sorry if this question sounds silly...

This is just the same point. We also need to add
the feature and documentation to RStan.

>> 1. We need to merge these into a single file
>>
>> where the mass is adapted in one case and set in the
>>
>> other case. I'd rather just call this nuts_mass
>>
>> and maybe change nuts_diag to nuts_mass_diag.
>>
>> Ideally, we'd also roll these two files together to
>>
>> cut down on cut-and-paste.

I can try to do this myself at some point. It's not critical
that it happens right away.

>> 2. We need to change the constructor in nuts_givenmass to
>>
>> take in either (a) a matrix, or (b) a var_context.
>>
>> it should be the job of the client to nuts_givenmass
>>
>
> I am also not sure what is a "var_context"... maybe we can talk more in the meeting next week. Actually the "mass_given" may not be very convenient to use because stan will implicitly transform the parameters, which makes user hard to set a covariance matrix because they need to think in terms of "transformed parameters".

stan::io::var_context is a base class implemented in Stan that
is a higher-level interface for I/O of structured data.
For instance, it's implemented in stan::io::dump to read
from an R-style dump-format file. It's implemented in RStan
to read from an R environment. The point is that we won't
always have a file -- we'll get the matrix in other ways and
we want to generalize the access.

- Bob

messages.author: ace9745b50e86915
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: refactoring nuts_givenmass and nuts_nondiag
parts: Actually I tried all the models that has been coded by Daniel, what I find is that for problems where dimension of parameters are smaller than 100, the non-diagonal mass matrix usually has better performance in terms of time/n_eff. Sometimes the benefit is great while most of the times it is similar to the default sampler. For higher dimension, the sampler does work but has lower time/n_eff than default stan. I am willing to try more alternatives on estimating the matrix, but I pushed the code because I think it does not affect the default sampler and at least it does work in some case. The result is attached. The last column of the table shows whether the non_diag perform better than diag sampler.
